# Residual

> Residual is an iPhone meal planner and tracker for people who eat to calorie and macro targets. You set each target with its own range, Claude drafts the day from what is in your pantry, you log what you actually ate, and a deterministic solver re-sizes the meals still ahead so the day lands inside your ranges.

Residual is made by Clark Sell. It runs on iOS 27 or later, iPhone only; there is no Android version and none on the near-term roadmap. It is a meal planner and tracker that competes with apps such as Cronometer, though it doesn't include every major food database (foods come from USDA FoodData Central and barcodes, and the user can add any food by photographing its Nutrition Facts label), and it has no dashboard for nutritionists or trainers; any day exports as a CSV.

## Key facts

- Platform: iPhone, iOS 27 or later. Works offline; planning with Claude and USDA food search need a connection.
- Targets: calories, protein, carbs and fat, each with its own plus-or-minus range. The user enters numbers from a coach or dietitian, or a built-in TDEE calculator works them out from body, activity and goal. Any one may float, meaning it is balanced last and never marks the day as off. Residual doesn't adjust targets from a weight trend.
- AI: Claude, from Anthropic, and Apple's on-device model. Neither sizes the final portions.
- Planning: Claude (through Apple's Foundation Models framework with App Attest) drafts meals, foods and grams, only if the user allows it. Otherwise the day is planned on the iPhone with Apple's on-device model, or from the user's pantry, saved meals and built-in foods. A switch, Only plan from my pantry, keeps every food in the plan to what the user has.
- Re-solving: when a logged meal differs from the plan, a deterministic solver (not AI) re-sizes the meals ahead by the smallest plausible change, keeping the same foods rather than swapping them, and the user sees every change before applying it: calories first, then protein, carbs and fat; every portion stays between about half and double its plan, in grams on a 5 g grid. When the ranges can't be met, the forecast says so.
- Logging: amounts start from the plan, so a meal eaten as planned is logged with one swipe; the user changes only what differed. Logging never overwrites the plan, and divergence from the plan is shown. Portions are stored in grams and can be shown in ounces, cups, tablespoons or millilitres, so a food scale helps but isn't required.
- Today: one calorie ring with five gauges the user taps through (Eaten, Landing, Left, Plan, Clock), bars for the macros, one sentence that says where the day lands, and one button for the next step.
- Widgets: six for the Home Screen and Lock Screen (Landing, Clock, Next Up, Eaten, Left, Plan). A widget's Log button opens the meal and never logs by itself.
- Recipes: a dish from weighed ingredients becomes one food, per 100 g, that can be planned, logged and shared.
- Not yet: no import from other trackers; Apple Health support is planned for a later version.
- Food data: USDA FoodData Central, matched by the user (never silently), with barcode scanning. AI estimates are labelled as estimates until matched.
- Privacy: data stays on the iPhone and in the user's private iCloud database. No account, no tracking, no analytics.
- Price: no free tier. Everything is part of Residual Plus, an auto-renewing App Store subscription: $14.99 a month, $39.99 every 3 months or $124.99 a year (US prices), each starting with a 14-day free trial. No ads, no data sold, no lifetime deal, no sales.
- Export: any day as a CSV of eaten and planned grams per food.

## Pages

- [Home](https://residual.fit/): what Residual does, a live demo of the solver, the five gauges and six widgets, and answers to common questions (weight loss, logging effort, food scales, targets, switching from another app)
- [Features](https://residual.fit/features/): everything the app does: Close the residual, AI day plans, planning ahead, your pantry, saved meals and recipes, logging, USDA foods and barcodes, grocery lists, the gauges and widgets, sharing, targets and privacy
- [Pricing](https://residual.fit/pricing/): what Residual costs and why: $14.99 a month, $39.99 a quarter or $124.99 a year, a 14-day trial, no free tier, and where the money goes (Claude and food data)
- [Help](https://residual.fit/help/): how to use Residual, one task to a page: setting daily targets, ranges and the landing order, closing the residual and recalibrating, and fixes for food search, barcodes and labels
- [Help and support](https://residual.fit/support/): the subscription, offline use, planning with Claude, your data, and fixes for common problems
- [Privacy policy](https://residual.fit/privacy/): what the app stores, what leaves the phone, who receives it, and how to delete it
- [Terms of use](https://residual.fit/terms/): the agreement with Unspecified LLC, which publishes Residual: adults 18 and older only, not medical advice, subscriptions billed and refunded through Apple, and individual arbitration under Illinois law with a 30-day opt-out
- [Health disclaimer](https://residual.fit/health-disclaimer/): the disclaimer every user agrees to in the app: Residual is not medical or nutrition advice, its numbers are estimates, check allergies and conditions with a doctor or registered dietitian first, and the user is responsible for what they eat
